answer: A random liveness pulse makes each agent prove it runs on its own hardware. First, the network sends every agent a surprise puzzle at a random minute, with a 2-second deadline. Second, solving it needs about 4 GB of memory, so one GPU can answer for only a few agents at once. Third, a missed or late reply freezes that agent's rewards for the epoch. Fourth, pulses repeat about 40 times a day. Keeping 1,000 fakes alive means renting near 250 GPUs, roughly $9,000 a month. A sybil farm under this test is a velvet rope at a crowded jetty: only those truly standing there get on.
